newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's TCV 1997/98 funding A$1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's TCV 1997/98 funding A$1.5 bln.

text.p: Treasury Corporation of Victoria said on Tuesday that its indicative funding programme for the year to June 30, 1998 would be A$1.5 billion and consist entirely of refinancing of maturities.

TCV, the borrowing arm of the state of Victoria, said that as indicated in Victoria's budget 1997/98 delivered earlier on Tuesday, the public sector net debt is projected to fall by A$700 million during the fiscal year, before allowing for the impact of further privatiations.

TCV estimates its net impact on markets during the 1996/97 financial year was a A$5.1 billion repayment after managing the receipt of A$7.1 billion in total proceeds from the government's privatisation programme and further reductions across the public sector.
TCv expects the net impact on financial markets for 1997/98 to be about A$800 million.

"TCV has made substantial progress in retiring debt and is well positioned to progressively apply the proceeds of Loy Yang A to debt maturities and early retirement upon receipt in mid-May," said David Carruthers, TCV's Managing Director.
The Victorian state government sold its Loy Yang Power assets for A$4.855 billion earlier this month.

"TCV's domestic Hot Stocks are our core funding instruments. We will ensure that our Hots Stocks maintain their status in the secondary market and support this by regular tenders, every six to eight weeks," Carruthers said.
"We constantly review our issuance strategies and adapt to changing circumstances," he added.
TCV will be hosting a budget address by the Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale to the financial markets in Melbourne and Sydney on May 1 and 2.
